title: A Virtual Element Method for elliptic problems on trimmed background meshes
summary: We consider a two-dimensional piecewise $C^2$ domain that cuts through a quasi-uniform fixed polygonal background mesh, for instance made of quadrilaterals. A simple procedure based on convex hulls gives rise to a rather small number of polygonal boundary elements of various shapes, including elements with small edges and large aspect ratios; this is the computational mesh for a virtual element method (VEM), a trimmed background mesh. We classify all possible geometric configurations and study their stability and approximability properties. This entails deriving robust stabilization…
